title: Reduced Layer Count for Manufacturing Tolerance
scientific_hypothesis: A reduced layer count stack will achieve acceptable dual-band performance while improving manufacturing yield and reducing stress-related defects.
design_principle: Fewer layers reduce cumulative stress, deposition time, and defect probability; if performance remains acceptable, the trade-off favors manufacturability for field-deployed cameras.
proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2 | sio2)_5 | sio2 substrate | 10 layers total
manufacturing_considerations: 10 layers is well below 30-layer limit, reducing deposition time
Lower cumulative stress reduces delamination risk
Fewer interfaces reduce scatter and absorption losses
theory_basis: Layer count vs. performance trade-off in dielectric filters
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient UV reflection with only 10 layers
SWIR transmission may be compromised if UV reflection is inadequate
Performance ceiling lower than higher-count stacks
execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: Air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Lemarchand))_5 | SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate, totaling 10 layers. Optimize the quarter-wave reference wavelength and a uniform thickness scale factor to maximize transmission in 1000-1700 nm band and reflection in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
